comparator.academicYear: 2026-2027 (Education and Examination Regulations BSc Circular Engineering, Faculty of Science and Engineering, in force 1 September 2026; programme pages checked 2026-10-03)
comparator.sourceNotes: The programme pages (s1, s2) describe the structure in words only: a common first year, a second year of electives, skills and projects, and a third year with one of four concentrations and a thesis; they give no course list with EC. The 180-EC reconstruction therefore uses the 2026-2027 Education and Examination Regulations (s0): Article 3.6 (study load per year), 3.7 (core), 3.8 (electives), 3.9 (concentration and thesis) and Appendix I (course overview). Year 1: eight mandatory 5-EC courses, 10 EC of skills courses and two 5-EC projects. Year 2: eight elective 5-EC courses and four elective 2.5-EC skills courses (two courses and one skill per period, chosen from the published framework) plus two mandatory 5-EC projects; the framework is availability-dependent, so one coherent valid selection linked to the Circular Chemical Engineering concentration is instantiated (Organic Chemistry, Fluid Mechanics, Numerical Methods, Polymeric Materials, Differential Equations, Biochemistry, Heat & Mass Transfer, Remake Reuse Repair Recycle; skills in organic chemistry, statistics, fabrication and design, and analytical and physical chemistry) and is flagged here as an instantiation of restricted choice rather than a fixed requirement. The Heat & Mass Transfer elective is explicitly linked to this concentration, which satisfies the requirement that one elective be linked to a third-year concentration. Year 3: one mandatory 5-EC core course (Ethical and Philosophical Reflections), the Circular Chemical Engineering concentration of five 5-EC courses (the fifth, Circular Process Design and Control, shown in the period 3-4 slot) and two 2.5-EC skills courses, and the 25-EC bachelor thesis (BTH3010). Totals are 60 EC per year and 180 EC overall.

alternatives.concept: Combine life-cycle analysis and circular-resource recovery with earth materials, geochemistry, soils, energy and environmental systems; add biochemistry, molecular-cell study and laboratory work; and use programming, calculus, linear algebra, probability and numerical methods to analyse those systems. This related-fields route does not provide chemical engineering, physics, thermodynamics, transport phenomena, reactor design or process engineering.

alternatives.labelRationale: The curriculum is led by circularity, environmental materials and earth systems, supported by seven mathematics, programming, statistics and research courses and four life-science courses. The label reflects the dominant content and does not claim an engineering degree.

alternatives.concept: Pursue the target's Sustainable Biotechnology direction through molecular and cell biology, biochemistry and laboratory work, then connect living systems to ecology, biodiversity, sustainable farming, environmental biogeochemistry, resource recovery and nature-based design, with statistics, data science, AI, spatial analysis and applied sustainability research. UCR offers no fermentation, enzyme engineering, bioreactor or industrial bioprocess sequence.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the first route, this programme replaces eight courses in advanced calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, programming, circular life-cycle analysis, soils, resources and renewable-system design with eight courses in biodiversity, conservation, sustainable farming, earth observation, nature-based design, data science, AI and sustainability governance. Each programme therefore contains 60 EC not present in the other.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The target is the generic bachelor and its third year offers four formal concentrations (Circular Chemical Engineering, Sustainable Biotechnology, Engineering Physics for Sustainable Manufacturing, Sustainable Mechanical Engineering), none of which is shown by current official evidence to be more representative of the programme's broad identity or less specialised than the others. The official curriculum page and the 2026-2027 Education and Examination Regulations list Circular Chemical Engineering first, and its year-1 chemical-engineering core and year-2 Heat & Mass Transfer link make it a coherent continuation of the common curriculum, so the neutral order tie-break selects it. The route was not chosen by reference to UCR course fit.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The historical judgment correctly identified the absent engineering spine but incorrectly treated that gap as excluding all related-fields responses. One coherent programme addresses circular materials, environmental systems and quantitative science; a second follows the formally evidenced Sustainable Biotechnology direction through life science, ecology and circular production. The next mechanical/manufacturing direction is infeasible because UCR lacks the required physics, mechanics, electronics, materials and engineering-design sequence, so production stops at two.

notes.text: Maastricht Circular Engineering combines a compulsory mathematics, physics, chemistry, biotechnology and engineering core with practical laboratories and design projects, then a specialist concentration and 25-EC engineering thesis. UCR can combine circularity, environmental materials, life science and quantitative methods, but these programmes offer related perspectives rather than a Circular Engineering degree.

UCR offers no sustained physics or chemistry sequence, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat and mass transfer, reactor or separation engineering, process control, fabrication, unit operations or engineering-design thesis. The quantitative and sustainability courses are not presented as substitutes for that engineering formation.
